description: 'North Star'. A prestigious Wuyi Rock Oolong cultivar directly descended from the legendary Da Hong Pao lineage. It is renowned for its powerful and robust character, thick body, and a classic roasted flavor profile that is both complex and deeply satisfying, making it a favorite among seasoned Yancha drinkers.
parentage: Cloned from the Bei Dou mother tree, which itself was said to be a cutting from an original Da Hong Pao bush.
also_known_as: North Star, Bei Dou Yi Hao (North Star #1)
plant_type: Sturdy, upright arbor type well-adapted to rocky terrain (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
optimal_environment: Grows best in the core 'Zhengyan' region of the Wuyi Mountains, where the mineral-rich soil and terroir create its powerful flavor.
tea_expressions: {"Wuyi Rock Oolong (Yancha)": {"Bei Dou Yancha": "A powerful, complex rock oolong with deep roast notes, a pronounced mineral character, and a long, sweet aftertaste."}}
sensory_footprint: {"aroma": "Roasted nuts, dark chocolate, subtle florals, warm minerals", "flavor": "Rich, robust, and deeply mineralic with a satisfying, lingering sweetness.", "mouthfeel_liquor": "Thick, viscous, and warming with a strong and comforting presence. The liquor is a deep, clear amber."}
processing_suitability_details: The processing of Bei Dou is a classic example of traditional Yancha craftsmanship. Its strong leaves can withstand the necessary heavy oxidation and multiple roasts that build its complex character.
oxidation_details: Undergoes heavy oxidation (50-60%) to develop a rich, fruity, and robust flavor base that serves as the perfect foundation for the charcoal roasting process.
roasting_details: Receives a medium-to-heavy charcoal roast, often in multiple stages. This is essential for creating its signature roasted depth, smoothing its texture, and developing the long, sweet finish.
style_versatility: Highly specialized. Bei Dou is a pure expression of the traditional, powerful Wuyi Rock Oolong style and is not used for other types of tea.

description: 'Osmanthus Fragrance'. A classic and beloved Phoenix Dan Cong oolong fragrance type. It is celebrated for its delicate, elegant, and very clear aroma of sweet osmanthus flowers. It is less overwhelmingly powerful than Mi Lan Xiang, offering a more refined and purely floral experience.
parentage: One of the ten traditional fragrance types, selected from the native Phoenix Mountain population.
plant_type: Medium-sized Dan Cong arbor (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
optimal_environment: Grows in the high-altitude, misty environment of the Phoenix Mountains, which allows for the slow development of its delicate aromatic compounds.
tea_expressions: {"Dan Cong Oolong": {"Gui Hua Xiang Dan Cong": "A medium-oxidized and lightly roasted Dan Cong, with processing focused on preserving its pure, singular osmanthus flower aroma."}}
sensory_footprint: {"aroma": "Clear and precise Sweet Osmanthus flower, hint of apricot", "flavor": "Delicate, sweet, and distinctly floral with a clean, refreshing finish.", "mouthfeel_liquor": "Silky, smooth, and clean with a light-to-medium body. The liquor is a clear, pale gold."}
processing_suitability_details: Processing Gui Hua Xiang requires a gentle hand. The goal is to highlight its specific, delicate fragrance without introducing any heavier, distracting notes. The withering and bruising steps are carefully managed to hit the perfect aromatic peak.
oxidation_details: Undergoes a light-to-medium oxidation (25-35%) to develop its floral character while maintaining a fresh and clean profile.
roasting_details: Receives a very light, low-temperature finishing roast. This is done to stabilize the tea and enhance its sweetness without adding any baked or roasted flavors that would mask the osmanthus scent.
style_versatility: Highly specialized. This is a classic fragrance profile within the Dan Cong oolong family and is not made in any other style.

description: 'Saw-leaf'. A rare, old-grove Dan Cong varietal from the Phoenix Mountains, named for the sharply serrated, saw-like edges of its leaves. It is a rustic and powerful tea, known for its wild, herbal, and stone fruit character, representing an older, less-manicured style of Dan Cong.
parentage: An old, native Phoenix Mountain varietal.
plant_type: Medium-sized Dan Cong arbor with distinctive, sharply serrated leaves (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
optimal_environment: Grows in the old tea gardens of the Phoenix Mountains, often from trees that are quite old. The specific terroir contributes to its rustic and deep flavor.
tea_expressions: {"Dan Cong Oolong": {"Ju Duo Zai Dan Cong": "A traditionally processed Dan Cong oolong where the processing aims to express its wild, deep, and untamed character."}}

The liquor is a deep golden-amber."}
processing_suitability_details: Processing this old-grove varietal follows traditional methods. The tea master aims to capture the full, complex character of the leaves rather than targeting a single, narrow fragrance profile.
oxidation_details: Undergoes a medium-to-heavy oxidation (40-55%) to develop its deep fruit notes and complex, rustic flavor base.
roasting_details: Typically receives a medium charcoal roast to integrate its powerful flavors, add depth, and ensure the tea will age well.
style_versatility: Highly specialized. Ju Duo Zai is a specific, old-style Dan Cong oolong appreciated for its rustic power and complexity.

description: A highly versatile Fujian cultivar, originally from Anxi. While it can be made into a pleasant oolong, it has gained modern fame as one of the primary cultivars used to produce Jin Jun Mei, an elite, bud-only black tea from the Wuyi region. Its inherent sweetness and fruity notes make it an excellent base for high-end black teas.
plant_type: Vigorous, semi-arbor type with good adaptability (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
optimal_environment: Highly adaptable to different terroirs within Fujian, which has contributed to its widespread use.

processing_suitability_details: Mei Zhan's versatility is due to its balanced chemical composition. Its buds are particularly well-suited for black tea processing, as they are rich in compounds that create sweetness and a thick texture when fully oxidized.
oxidation_details: Oxidation is typically full (100%) for its most famous black tea expression. When made as an oolong, it undergoes medium oxidation (30-40%).
roasting_details: Roasting is not a key feature. Black tea expressions are simply dried. Oolong expressions may receive a light bake.
style_versatility: Extremely versatile. It is a rare cultivar that can be skillfully crafted into high-quality oolong, black, and even white tea, though its modern fame is overwhelmingly tied to black tea.

description: 'Rare Orchid' or 'Marvelous Orchid'. A highly aromatic cultivar that originated in southern Fujian but has found a second home in the Wuyi Mountains. It is celebrated for its powerful and persistent orchid-like fragrance, which it can express beautifully as both a greener Anxi-style oolong and a more robust, roasted Wuyi-style rock oolong.
parentage: Originated in Pinghe County, southern Fujian.
plant_type: Upright, vigorous bush with good productivity (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
optimal_environment: Highly adaptable, it thrives in both the clay soils of its native southern Fujian and the rocky terroir of the Wuyi Mountains.
tea_expressions: {"Wuyi Rock Oolong (Yancha)": {"Qi Lan Yancha": "When grown in Wuyi, it's made into an aroma-forward rock oolong, balancing its orchid fragrance with a mineral base and a light-to-medium roast."}, "Anxi Oolong": {"Qi Lan Oolong": "When processed in Anxi, it is made in a greener, unroasted style that maximizes its intense, fresh floral aroma."}}

The liquor ranges from pale gold (Anxi style) to amber (Wuyi style)."}
processing_suitability_details: The processing style for Qi Lan depends entirely on the region. In Wuyi, it undergoes a traditional Yancha process with a moderate roast. In Anxi, it is processed very lightly like a modern Tie Guan Yin to preserve its fresh aroma.
oxidation_details: Oxidation ranges from light (20-30% for Anxi style) to medium (40-50% for Wuyi style), demonstrating the cultivar's ability to adapt to different processing goals.
roasting_details: Roasting is the key differentiator. It is unroasted in Anxi to preserve fresh florals, but receives a light-to-medium charcoal roast in Wuyi to add depth and a mineral character.
style_versatility: Very versatile within the oolong category. It is one of the few cultivars that is famous for being produced in two distinct regional styles (Anxi and Wuyi).

description: 'Sparrow's Tongue'. A rare and highly sought-after Wuyi Rock Oolong named for its small, pointed leaves. It is celebrated for its exceptionally refined and elegant character, a high, sharp floral fragrance, and a very clean, mineral-driven taste. It is often processed with a lighter roast to preserve its delicate nature.
parentage: A prized selection from the native Wuyi heirloom population.
plant_type: Small-leaf, slow-growing, semi-upright bush (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
optimal_environment: Grows in specific, protected microclimates within the Wuyi Mountains. It is less common due to its lower yield and more demanding growing conditions.
tea_expressions: {"Wuyi Rock Oolong (Yancha)": {"Que She Yancha": "A highly refined and aromatic rock oolong, often with a lighter roast to preserve its delicate and penetrating floral notes."}}
sensory_footprint: {"aroma": "High, sharp, and lingering white flowers (gardenia, jasmine), very clean", "flavor": "Elegant, sweet, mineral-driven, and exceptionally clean with a vibrant finish.", "mouthfeel_liquor": "Silky, medium-bodied, and bright with a very pure texture. The liquor is a luminous golden-amber."}
processing_suitability_details: Processing Que She requires great finesse. The goal is to highlight its delicate, high-pitched aroma. The leaves, while small, are robust enough for Yancha processing but shine when handled with a lighter touch.
oxidation_details: Undergoes a standard medium oxidation (30-50%) to develop a base of flavor that supports, rather than overwhelms, its high-note aromatics.
roasting_details: Roasting is typically lighter than for other top-tier Yancha. A careful, low-temperature bake is used to bring out the mineral notes and add smoothness while preserving the vibrant floral fragrance.
style_versatility: Highly specialized. Que She is an expression of a more elegant and aromatic style of Wuyi Rock Oolong.

description: 'Heavenly Aroma' or 'Heaven-Reaching Aroma'. An old and highly revered Dan Cong cultivar from Wudong Mountain, the highest peak of the Phoenix range. It is known for its exceptionally powerful, penetrating, and complex aroma, often with notes of ginger and exotic spices, and a very strong 'cha qi' (tea energy).
parentage: An old, native Phoenix Mountain varietal from Wudong Mountain.
plant_type: Old Dan Cong arbor, often with a tall, upright growth habit (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
optimal_environment: Grows exclusively on the high slopes of Wudong Mountain, where the unique terroir is responsible for its incredible power and aromatic complexity.
tea_expressions: {"Dan Cong Oolong": {"Tong Tian Xiang Dan Cong": "A 'grand cru' Dan Cong oolong, processed with masterful skill to showcase its potent and multi-layered aromatic profile."}}

processing_suitability_details: Processing this elite cultivar requires the highest level of skill. The tea master must carefully guide the leaves through a complex withering and oxidation process to build its signature multi-layered aroma.
oxidation_details: Undergoes a deep and carefully controlled oxidation (40-60%) to develop the full spectrum of its complex aromatics, from spicy to fruity to floral.
roasting_details: Receives a masterful charcoal roast. The roast must be precise and deep enough to integrate the tea's powerful flavors and create a smooth texture, without damaging the prized aromatic compounds.
style_versatility: The ultimate specialist. Tong Tian Xiang is a rare, high-end Dan Cong oolong that represents the pinnacle of the style.
